question: If in acute-angled triangle ABC, AL, BM, and CN are the three altitudes of triangle ABC, then which of the following statements will be true?

options.text: AL + BM + CN = AB + BC + CA
AL + BM + CN > AB + BC + CA
AL + BM + CN < AB + BC + CA

solution:
**Given**

AL, BM, and CN are the three altitudes of triangle ABC

**Concept used**

The side opposite to the greater angle is a greater

**Calculation**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c2420f8cac2e931136a4e93a2c024eef6f5f150e3a81077bf792f056a121eb12.png] 

In the above diagram,

∠ALB = 90

∠ABL 

Now side opposite to ∠ALB is AB and the side opposite to ∠ABL is AL

Since the side opposite to the greater angle is a greater

AB > AL ..(1)

Similarly in triangle BMC

BC > BM ..(2)

Similarly in triangle ANC

CA > CN ..(3)

Adding all three:

AL + BM + CN 

**The answer is AL + BM + CN **
